Socioeconomic Portrait of Marin County, 2005-2025

Author

Thomas A. Petroff

Published

November 9, 2026

Population Growth in Marin County, 2005-2025

Between 2005 and 2025, Marin County has grown by about 4%. Much of the growth experienced during this period occurred during the first decade, when Marin County reached a peak total population of ~261,000 residents. Since 2015, this growth trend has reversed as the region has observed a decline.

#########
# Author: Thomas Petroff, RA - HPRC
# Date created: 06/06/2026
# Date last edited: 06/08/2026
# Project: Demographic Portrait of Marin County

## DESCRIPTION ##
# This R script is used to investigate demographic indicators for 
# Marin County spanning from 2005 - 2024 using 1-year ACS estimates

## SUBJECT TABLES OF INTEREST

# B01001 = Sex by Age
# B05013 = Sex by Age for the Foreign-born Population (data gathering initiated in 2014)
# B03002 = Hispanic or Latino Origin by Race
# B25003 = owner vs. renter occupied
# B11001 = Household type
# B11005 = Households with children (under 18)
# B17001 = Poverty Status in the past 12 months by Sex and Age
# B05006 = Place of Birth for the Foreign-born Population
# B05001 = Nativity and Citizenship Status in the United States
# B19013 = Median household income in the past 12 months (inflation-adjusted USD)
# B19001 = Median household income in the past 12 months - Income Brackets (inflation-adjusted USD)
# B19080: Household income quintile upper limits

# census_api_key("YOUR_KEY_HERE", install = TRUE)
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)
library(scales)

# 1. DEFINE VARIABLES
# We use standard ACS variable names. tidycensus will return these with an "E" suffix for estimates.
acs_vars <- c(
  # Total Population
  total_pop          = "B01001_001",
  
  # Race & Ethnicity
  nh_white           = "B03002_003",
  nh_black           = "B03002_004",
  nh_native_american = "B03002_005",
  nh_asian           = "B03002_006",
  hispanic_total     = "B03002_012",
  
  # Nativity & Citizenship
  pop_nativity_total = "B05001_001",
  born_in_us         = "B05001_002",
  naturalized_cit    = "B05001_005",
  non_citizen        = "B05001_006",
  
  # Housing
  housing_total      = "B25003_001",
  owner_occupied     = "B25003_002",
  renter_occupied    = "B25003_003",
  
  # Households
  total_households   = "B11001_001",
  married_couple_hh  = "B11001_003",
  one_person_nonfamily = "B11001_008",
  two_plus_nonfamily   = "B11001_009",
  hh_with_kids       = "B11005_002",
  
  # Poverty
  poverty_universe   = "B17001_001",
  below_poverty_line = "B17001_002",
  
  # Income & Brackets
  median_hh_income   = "B19013_001",
  inc_less_10k       = "B19001_002",
  inc_10k_14k        = "B19001_003",
  inc_15k_19k        = "B19001_004",
  inc_20k_24k        = "B19001_005",
  inc_25k_29k        = "B19001_006",
  inc_30k_34k        = "B19001_007",
  inc_35k_39k        = "B19001_008",
  inc_40k_44k        = "B19001_009",
  inc_45k_49k        = "B19001_010",
  inc_50k_59k        = "B19001_011",
  inc_60k_74k        = "B19001_012",
  inc_75k_99k        = "B19001_013",
  inc_100k_124k      = "B19001_014",
  inc_125k_149k      = "B19001_015",
  inc_150k_199k      = "B19001_016",
  inc_200k_up        = "B19001_017"
)

# 2. DEFINE YEARS (EXCLUDING 2020)
# This creates 2005 to 2024 but explicitly drops 2020
years <- setdiff(2005:2025, 2020)

marin_county <- map_dfr(years, function(y) {
  message(paste("Pulling County data for year:", y))
  
  # 1. Pull key indicators
  indicators <- get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    variables = acs_vars,
    year = y,
    survey = "acs1", 
    output = "wide"
  ) %>% 
    filter(GEOID == "06041") %>% 
    mutate(yr = y)
  
  # 2. Pull full B01001 for Age calculations
  age_table <- get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    table = "B01001",
    year = y,
    survey = "acs1",
    output = "wide"
  ) %>% 
    filter(GEOID == "06041") %>% 
    mutate(yr = y)
  
  # 3. Pull full B17001 for Child/Senior Poverty calculations
  poverty_table <- get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    table = "B17001",
    year = y,
    survey = "acs1",
    output = "wide"
  ) %>% 
    filter(GEOID == "06041") %>% 
    mutate(yr = y)
  
  # 4. Pull full B11001 for gendered householders
  hh_table <- get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    table = "B11001",
    year = y,
    survey = "acs1",
    output = "wide"
  ) %>% 
    filter(GEOID == "06041") %>% 
    mutate(yr = y)
  
  # Isolate Estimate columns for core merge
  indicators_clean <- indicators %>% select(yr, ends_with("E"))
  age_clean        <- age_table %>% select(yr, ends_with("E"))
  poverty_clean    <- poverty_table %>% select(yr, ends_with("E"))
  hh_clean         <- hh_table %>% select(yr, ends_with("E"))
  
  combined <- indicators_clean %>%
    left_join(age_clean, by = "yr") %>%
    left_join(poverty_clean, by = "yr") %>%
    left_join(hh_clean, by = "yr")
  
  # ========================================================
  # CONDITIONAL PULL FOR B05013 (Foreign-born Age Table)
  # ========================================================
  if (y >= 2014) {
    fb_age_table <- get_acs(
      geography = "county",
      table = "B05013",
      year = y,
      survey = "acs1",
      output = "wide"
    ) %>% 
      filter(GEOID == "06041") %>%
      select(ends_with("E")) # Isolate estimate columns
    
    combined <- bind_cols(combined, fb_age_table)
  } else {
    fb_cols <- setNames(rep(list(NA_real_), 39), paste0("B05013_", sprintf("%03d", 1:39), "E"))
    combined <- combined %>% mutate(!!!fb_cols)
  }
  
  return(combined)
})

# Clean up trailing 'E' from column names
names(marin_county) <- gsub("E$", "", names(marin_county))

# COUNTY DATA MANIPULATIONS
df_analysis_marin_county <- marin_county %>%
  mutate(
    # ========================================================
    # 1. TOTAL POPULATION 5-YEAR AGE BINS (Table B01001)
    # ========================================================
    # --- MALE TOTAL BINS ---
    m_00_04 = B01001_003,
    m_05_09 = B01001_004,
    m_10_14 = B01001_005,
    m_15_19 = B01001_006 + B01001_007,                 # 15-17 + 18-19
    m_20_24 = B01001_008 + B01001_009 + B01001_010,     # 20 + 21 + 22-24
    m_25_29 = B01001_011,
    m_30_34 = B01001_012,
    m_35_39 = B01001_013,
    m_40_44 = B01001_014,
    m_45_49 = B01001_015,
    m_50_54 = B01001_016,
    m_55_59 = B01001_017,
    m_60_64 = B01001_018 + B01001_019,                 # 60-61 + 62-64
    m_65_69 = B01001_020 + B01001_021,                 # 65-66 + 67-69
    m_70_74 = B01001_022,
    m_75_79 = B01001_023,
    m_80_84 = B01001_024,
    m_85_up = B01001_025,
    
    # --- FEMALE TOTAL BINS ---
    f_00_04 = B01001_027,
    f_05_09 = B01001_028,
    f_10_14 = B01001_029,
    f_15_19 = B01001_030 + B01001_031,                 # 15-17 + 18-19
    f_20_24 = B01001_032 + B01001_033 + B01001_034,     # 20 + 21 + 22-24
    f_25_29 = B01001_035,
    f_30_34 = B01001_036,
    f_35_39 = B01001_037,
    f_40_44 = B01001_038,
    f_45_49 = B01001_039,
    f_50_54 = B01001_040,
    f_55_59 = B01001_041,
    f_60_64 = B01001_042 + B01001_043,                 # 60-61 + 62-64
    f_65_69 = B01001_044 + B01001_045,                 # 65-66 + 67-69
    f_70_74 = B01001_046,
    f_75_79 = B01001_047,
    f_80_84 = B01001_048,
    f_85_up = B01001_049,
    
    # ========================================================
    # 2. FOREIGN-BORN 5-YEAR AGE BINS (Table B05013)
    # ========================================================
    # --- MALE FOREIGN-BORN BINS ---
    fb_m_00_04 = B05013_003,
    fb_m_05_09 = B05013_004,
    fb_m_10_14 = B05013_005,
    fb_m_15_19 = B05013_006,
    fb_m_20_24 = B05013_007,
    fb_m_25_29 = B05013_008,
    fb_m_30_34 = B05013_009,
    fb_m_35_39 = B05013_010,
    fb_m_40_44 = B05013_011,
    fb_m_45_49 = B05013_012,
    fb_m_50_54 = B05013_013,
    fb_m_55_59 = B05013_014,
    fb_m_60_64 = B05013_015, 
    fb_m_65_69 = B05013_016,
    fb_m_70_74 = B05013_017,
    fb_m_75_79 = B05013_036,
    fb_m_80_84 = B05013_037,
    fb_m_85_up = B05013_038,
    
    # --- FEMALE FOREIGN-BORN BINS ---
    fb_f_00_04 = B05013_022,
    fb_f_05_09 = B05013_023,
    fb_f_10_14 = B05013_024,
    fb_f_15_19 = B05013_025,
    fb_f_20_24 = B05013_026,
    fb_f_25_29 = B05013_027,
    fb_f_30_34 = B05013_028,
    fb_f_35_39 = B05013_029,
    fb_f_40_44 = B05013_030,
    fb_f_45_49 = B05013_031,
    fb_f_50_54 = B05013_032,
    fb_f_55_59 = B05013_033,
    fb_f_60_64 = B05013_034, 
    fb_f_65_69 = B05013_035,
    fb_f_70_74 = B05013_039,
    fb_f_75_79 = B05013_036,
    fb_f_80_84 = B05013_037,
    fb_f_85_up = B05013_038,
    
    # ========================================================
    # 3. MACRO DEMOGRAPHIC GROUPS & HOUSING
    # ========================================================
    total_age_00_17           = (m_00_04 + m_05_09 + m_10_14 + B01001_006) + (f_00_04 + f_05_09 + f_10_14 + B01001_030),
    male_age_00_17            = (m_00_04 + m_05_09 + m_10_14 + B01001_006),
    female_age_00_17          = (f_00_04 + f_05_09 + f_10_14 + B01001_030),
    total_age_18_64           = (B01001_007 + m_20_24 + m_25_29 + m_30_34 + m_35_39 + m_40_44 + m_45_49 + m_50_54 + m_55_59 + m_60_64) + (B01001_031 + f_20_24 + f_25_29 + f_30_34 + f_35_39 + f_40_44 + f_45_49 + f_50_54 + f_55_59 + f_60_64),
    male_age_18_64            = (B01001_007 + m_20_24 + m_25_29 + m_30_34 + m_35_39 + m_40_44 + m_45_49 + m_50_54 + m_55_59 + m_60_64),
    female_age_18_64          = (B01001_031 + f_20_24 + f_25_29 + f_30_34 + f_35_39 + f_40_44 + f_45_49 + f_50_54 + f_55_59 + f_60_64),
    total_age_65_plus         = (m_65_69 + m_70_74 + m_75_79 + m_80_84 + m_85_up) + (f_65_69 + f_70_74 + f_75_79 + f_80_84 + f_85_up),
    male_age_65_plus          = (m_65_69 + m_70_74 + m_75_79 + m_80_84 + m_85_up),
    female_age_65_plus        = (f_65_69 + f_70_74 + f_75_79 + f_80_84 + f_85_up),
    male_pop                  = male_age_00_17 + male_age_18_64 + male_age_65_plus,
    female_pop                = female_age_00_17 + female_age_18_64 + female_age_65_plus,
    nh_other                  = total_pop - (hispanic_total + nh_white + nh_black + nh_asian + nh_native_american),
    foreign_born_count        = naturalized_cit + non_citizen,
    male_other_family_hh      = B11001_005, 
    female_other_family_hh    = B11001_006,
    poverty_child_count       = (B17001_004 + B17001_005 + B17001_006 + B17001_007 + B17001_008 + B17001_009) + (B17001_018 + B17001_019 + B17001_020 + B17001_021 + B17001_022 + B17001_023),
    poverty_senior_count      = (B17001_015 + B17001_016) + (B17001_029 + B17001_030),
    poverty_working_age_count = below_poverty_line - (poverty_child_count + poverty_senior_count)
  ) %>%
  
  # ========================================================
# 4. EXPLICIT SELECTION AND COLUMN ORDERING
# ========================================================
select(
  yr, total_pop, male_pop, female_pop,
  
  # Total Pop Pyramid Intervals (Preceding)
  m_00_04, m_05_09, m_10_14, m_15_19, m_20_24, m_25_29, m_30_34, m_35_39, m_40_44, m_45_49, m_50_54, m_55_59, m_60_64, m_65_69, m_70_74, m_75_79, m_80_84, m_85_up,
  f_00_04, f_05_09, f_10_14, f_15_19, f_20_24, f_25_29, f_30_34, f_35_39, f_40_44, f_45_49, f_50_54, f_55_59, f_60_64, f_65_69, f_70_74, f_75_79, f_80_84, f_85_up,
  
  # Foreign-Born Pyramid Intervals (Following)
  fb_m_00_04, fb_m_05_09, fb_m_10_14, fb_m_15_19, fb_m_20_24, fb_m_25_29, fb_m_30_34, fb_m_35_39, fb_m_40_44, fb_m_45_49, fb_m_50_54, fb_m_55_59, fb_m_60_64, fb_m_65_69, fb_m_70_74, fb_m_75_79, fb_m_80_84, fb_m_85_up,
  fb_f_00_04, fb_f_05_09, fb_f_10_14, fb_f_15_19, fb_f_20_24, fb_f_25_29, fb_f_30_34, fb_f_35_39, fb_f_40_44, fb_f_45_49, fb_f_50_54, fb_f_55_59, fb_f_60_64, fb_f_65_69, fb_f_70_74, fb_f_75_79, fb_f_80_84, fb_f_85_up,
  
  # Macro Structural Metrics
  total_age_00_17, total_age_18_64, total_age_65_plus, 
  male_age_00_17, male_age_18_64, male_age_65_plus, 
  female_age_00_17, female_age_18_64, female_age_65_plus,
  nh_white, nh_black, nh_asian, nh_native_american, nh_other, hispanic_total, foreign_born_count,
  housing_total, owner_occupied, renter_occupied, total_households, married_couple_hh, 
  male_other_family_hh, female_other_family_hh, one_person_nonfamily, two_plus_nonfamily, hh_with_kids,
  poverty_universe, below_poverty_line, poverty_child_count, poverty_senior_count, poverty_working_age_count,
  median_hh_income, starts_with("inc_")
)

# 2. Render Plot
ggplot(df_analysis_marin_county, aes(x = yr, y = total_pop)) +
  geom_line(color = "#004c6d", linewidth = 1.8) + 
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_comma(),
    breaks = pretty_breaks(n = 6)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2005:2025) + 
  # Safe axis zoom: zooms the panel without clipping data or line geometry
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(240000, 265000), expand = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Population Trend: Marin County",
    subtitle = "Annual 1-Year ACS baseline (2005–2025)",
    caption = "Data source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year Estimates. Note: 2005 reflects household population; 2020 omitted.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total Population"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "grey30", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, face = "plain"),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 20, b = 10, l = 10)
  )

# 4. JOIN AND PIVOT INTO LONG FORMAT
marin_cities_long <- pop_2005_2009 %>%
  left_join(pop_2010_2019, by = c("city_name", "geoid")) %>%
  left_join(pop_2020_2025, by = c("city_name", "geoid")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("yr"),
    names_to = "yr",
    names_prefix = "yr",
    values_to = "total_pop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(yr = as.numeric(yr))

# 5. ISOLATE ENDPOINT (2025) FOR DIRECT LINE LABELS
df_labels <- marin_cities_long %>%
  filter(yr == 2025)

# 6. DEFINE PLOTTING FUNCTION
plot_marin_cities_growth <- function(df, df_end_labels) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = yr, y = total_pop, color = city_name)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
    # Bold end-of-line labels positioned outside 2025 using ggrepel
    geom_text_repel(
      data = df_end_labels,
      aes(label = city_name),
      fontface = "bold",
      size = 3.8,
      hjust = 0,
      nudge_x = 0.5,
      direction = "y",
      segment.color = "grey70",
      segment.size = 0.4,
      xlim = c(2025.2, 2029.5)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 65000),
      labels = scales::label_comma(),
      breaks = seq(0, 65000, by = 5000)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(2005, 2025, by = 1),
      limits = c(2005, 2030),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0))
    ) +
    scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
    labs(
      title = "Population Trends: Marin County Municipalities",
      subtitle = "Annual Population Estimates (2005–2025)",
      caption = "Data source: U.S. Census Bureau Population Estimates Program (PEP).",
      x = "",

    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      legend.position = "none" # Suppress legend in favor of direct end-of-line labels
    )

Population Pyramid Series, Marin County (2005-2025)

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)
library(scales)

# --- 1. Reshape Total Population for Pyramid ---
df_marin_binned <- df_analysis_marin_county %>%
  select(yr, starts_with("m_"), starts_with("f_")) %>%
  select(-starts_with("fb_")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -yr,
    names_to = "group",
    values_to = "count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Sex = ifelse(substr(group, 1, 1) == "m", "Male", "Female"),
    Age_Group = gsub("_", "-", substr(group, 3, nchar(group))),
    Age_Group = ifelse(Age_Group == "85-up", "85+", Age_Group)
  ) %>%
  mutate(Age_Group = factor(Age_Group, levels = c(
    "00-04", "05-09", "10-14", "15-19", "20-24", "25-29", "30-34", "35-39", 
    "40-44", "45-49", "50-54", "55-59", "60-64", "65-69", "70-74", 
    "75-79", "80-84", "85+"
  )))

# --- 2. Prep Plotting Coordinates ---
df_marin_plot <- df_marin_binned %>%
  mutate(plot_count = ifelse(Sex == "Male", -count, count))

p_marin_pyr <- ggplot(df_marin_plot, aes(x = Age_Group, y = plot_count, fill = Sex)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) comma(abs(x)),
    breaks = c(-12000, -6000, 0, 6000, 12000),
    limits = c(-12000, 12000)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Male" = "#004c6d", "Female" = "#de425b")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Marin County Total Population Profile: {frame_time}",
    x = "Age Cohort",
    y = "Population Count",
    caption = "Data source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year Estimates"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, face = "italic", color = "grey40", hjust = 0),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  transition_time(as.integer(yr)) +
  ease_aes('linear')

# --- 3. Render Animation ---
animate(
  p_marin_pyr, 
  nframes = 400,          # Increased frame count for smoother transitions
  fps = 10, 
  duration = 32,          # Extended duration to 32 seconds
  end_pause = 60,         # Pause at end frame before looping
  width = 900, 
  height = 750, 
  units = "px", 
  res = 110,
  renderer = gifski_renderer()
)

Changes in Household Structure

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Define color scheme in exact legend order (Top to Bottom)
marin_census_colors <- c(
  "One person, nonfamily"            = "#08306b", 
  "Two or more people, nonfamily"    = "#2171b5", 
  "Male householder, other family"   = "#6baed6", 
  "Female householder, other family" = "#999999", 
  "Married couple households"        = "#d9d9d9"
)

# 2. Extract and calculate household structure for Marin County
df_marin_hh_structure <- df_analysis_marin_county %>%
  filter(yr %in% c(2005, 2015, 2025)) %>% 
  rename(year = yr) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(total_households, married_couple_hh, male_other_family_hh, 
             female_other_family_hh, one_person_nonfamily, two_plus_nonfamily), 
           \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `One person, nonfamily`            = round((one_person_nonfamily / total_households) * 100, 1),
    `Two or more people, nonfamily`    = round((two_plus_nonfamily / total_households) * 100, 1),
    `Male householder, other family`   = round((male_other_family_hh / total_households) * 100, 1),
    `Female householder, other family` = round((female_other_family_hh / total_households) * 100, 1),
    `Married couple households`        = round((married_couple_hh / total_households) * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(year, total_households, 
         `One person, nonfamily`, 
         `Two or more people, nonfamily`, 
         `Male householder, other family`, 
         `Female householder, other family`, 
         `Married couple households`)

# 3. Pivot and strictly order levels (Married = Bottom, One Person = Top)
df_marin_hh_plot_data <- df_marin_hh_structure %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(year, total_households),
    names_to = "household_type",
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    household_type = fct_relevel(household_type, 
                                 "Married couple households",
                                 "Female householder, other family",
                                 "Male householder, other family",
                                 "Two or more people, nonfamily",
                                 "One person, nonfamily"),
    label_color = ifelse(household_type %in% c("One person, nonfamily", "Two or more people, nonfamily"), 
                         "white", "black")
  )

# 4. Generate the Stacked Bar Plot
ggplot(df_marin_hh_plot_data, aes(x = factor(year), y = percentage, fill = household_type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.65, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = marin_census_colors, breaks = names(marin_census_colors)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", percentage), group = household_type, color = label_color), 
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
            size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  labs(
    title = "Household Structure Profile: Marin County",
    caption = "Data source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year Estimates",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 20)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", margin = margin(t = 15), hjust = 1)
  )

Median Household Income, 2020-2024 period

Code 
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(tidycensus)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# 1. Define Marin County FIPS & State
marin_fips <- "041"
state_code <- "CA"

# 2. Pull 2024 ACS 5-Year Tract Data (B19013_001 = Median Household Income)
marin_tracts_24 <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = state_code,
  county = marin_fips,
  variables = c(med_income = "B19013_001"),
  year = 2024,
  survey = "acs5",
  geometry = TRUE,
  output = "wide"
) %>%
  mutate(
    income_cat = cut(
      med_incomeE,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 75000, 125000, 200000, Inf),
      labels = c("< $75k", "$75k to $124.9k", "$125k to $199.9k", "$200k+"),
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  )

# 3. Pull County Boundary
marin_county_bounds_24 <- counties(
  state = state_code, 
  cb = TRUE, 
  year = 2024
) %>%
  filter(COUNTYFP == marin_fips)

# 4. Pull Primary & Secondary Highways
marin_highways_24 <- primary_secondary_roads(
  state = state_code, 
  year = 2024
) %>%
  st_crop(st_bbox(marin_county_bounds_24)) %>%
  filter(RTTYP %in% c("I", "U", "S"))

# 5. Calculate Bounding Box with a 5% Buffer
marin_bbox_24 <- st_bbox(marin_county_bounds_24)
x_span_24 <- marin_bbox_24["xmax"] - marin_bbox_24["xmin"]
y_span_24 <- marin_bbox_24["ymax"] - marin_bbox_24["ymin"]

tight_xlim_24 <- c(marin_bbox_24["xmin"] - (x_span_24 * 0.05), marin_bbox_24["xmax"] + (x_span_24 * 0.05))
tight_ylim_24 <- c(marin_bbox_24["ymin"] - (y_span_24 * 0.05), marin_bbox_24["ymax"] + (y_span_24 * 0.05))

# 6. Generate 2024 Map
p_map_income_24 <- ggplot() +
  # Choropleth Tracts
  geom_sf(
    data = marin_tracts_24,
    aes(fill = income_cat),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  # Major Highway Overlay
  geom_sf(
    data = marin_highways_24,
    aes(color = "Major Highways"),
    linewidth = 0.55,
    alpha = 0.8,
    key_glyph = draw_key_path
  ) +
  # County Boundary
  geom_sf(
    data = marin_county_bounds_24,
    aes(color = "County Boundary"),
    fill = NA,
    linewidth = 1.1,
    key_glyph = draw_key_path
  ) +
  # Custom Fill Palette (Greens for Income)
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Median Household Income",
    values = c(
      "< $75k"          = "#C7E9C0",
      "$75k to $124.9k" = "#74C476",
      "$125k to $199.9k"= "#238B45",
      "$200k+"          = "#00441B"
    ),
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  # Custom Line Palette
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Map Features",
    values = c(
      "County Boundary" = "black",
      "Major Highways"  = "grey20"
    ),
    guide = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(linewidth = c(1.1, 0.55))
    )
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = tight_xlim_24,
    ylim = tight_ylim_24,
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Household Income by Census Tract",
    subtitle = "Marin County, CA (2024 ACS 5-Year Estimates)",
    caption = "Data source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 5-Year Estimates (Table B19013)"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.7, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0, color = "grey30"),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey40", hjust = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(order = 1),
    color = guide_legend(order = 2)
  )

# Display 2024 Map
print(p_map_income_24)

Changes in Industries of Employment

The Browning-Singelmann framework:

  • Producer Services (Finance, Insurance, Real Estate, Legal, Accounting, Management, Engineering & Technical Consulting)

  • Social Services (Healthcare & Social Assistance, Educational Services, Public Administration, Non-Profit Organizations)

  • Personal Services (Food Services & Accommodations, Arts & Entertainment, Recreation, Household Services, Repair & Maintenance)

  • Distributive Services (Retail & Wholesale Trade, Transportation, Warehousing, Utilities, Logistics)

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggthemes)
library(haven)

# setwd("C:/Users/tap6/OneDrive - Rice University/Desktop/Marin County")

ipums_marin_data_extract <- read_dta("ipums_marin_data_extract.dta")

### DATA CLEANING ###
# Let's remove 2020 census data because the weights are disproportionally affected
ipums_marin_data_extract <- ipums_marin_data_extract %>% 
  filter(year != 2020)

# Restrict data to prime-working-age population (25-64) AND actively employed (empstat == 1)
ipums_marin_data_extract <- ipums_marin_data_extract %>%
  filter(age >= 25 & age <= 64, empstat == 1) 

# print(ipums_marin_data_extract)

#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggthemes)
library(haven)

# setwd("C:/Users/tap6/OneDrive - Rice University/Desktop/Marin County")

ipums_marin_data_extract <- read_dta("ipums_marin_data_extract.dta")

### DATA CLEANING ###
# Let's remove 2020 census data because the weights are disproportionally affected
ipums_marin_data_extract <- ipums_marin_data_extract %>% 
  filter(year != 2020)

# Restrict data to prime-working-age population (25-64) AND actively employed (empstat == 1)
ipums_marin_data_extract <- ipums_marin_data_extract %>%
  filter(age >= 25 & age <= 64, empstat == 1) 

# print(ipums_marin_data_extract, n = 10)

plot_industry_trends_clean <- ipums_marin_data_extract %>%
  # Filter out 2020 pandemic sampling anomaly
  filter(year != 2020) %>%
  # Filter for Marin County (FIPS 41), Age 25-64, and Actively Employed (empstat == 1)
  filter(
    as.numeric(countyfip) == 41,
    as.numeric(age) >= 25 & as.numeric(age) <= 64,
    as.numeric(empstat) == 1
  ) %>%
  # Convert year to numeric vector
  mutate(year_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(year))) %>%
  # Calculate total annual weighted workforce for Marin County
  group_by(year_numeric) %>%
  mutate(yearly_total = sum(perwt, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  # Map IPUMS IND codes to Browning-Singelmann Macro Sectors
  mutate(
    macro_sector = case_when(
      # Construction & Agriculture
      ind == 770 ~ "Construction",
      ind >= 170 & ind <= 290 ~ "Agriculture",
      
      # 1. Distributive Services (Logistics & Trade)
      (ind >= 6070 & ind <= 6390) | (ind >= 6470 & ind <= 6780) ~ "Distributive Services",
      
      # 2. Producer Services (B2B & Professional)
      (ind >= 6870 & ind <= 6990) | (ind >= 7270 & ind <= 7590) | 
        ind %in% c(7070, 7080, 7170, 7190, 7670) ~ "Producer Services",
      
      # 3. Social Services (Health, Education & Government)
      (ind >= 7860 & ind <= 7890) | (ind >= 7970 & ind <= 8470) | 
        (ind >= 0570 & ind <= 0690) | (ind >= 9370 & ind <= 9590) | 
        ind %in% c(7790, 9160, 9170, 9180, 9190) ~ "Social Services",
      
      # 4. Personal Services (Hospitality, Facilities & Repair)
      (ind >= 8560 & ind <= 8690) | (ind >= 8970 & ind <= 9090) | 
        (ind >= 8770 & ind <= 8880) | ind %in% c(7680, 7690, 7770, 7780, 9290, 7180) ~ "Personal Services",
      
      # Catch-all
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Aggregate weighted estimates by macro sector and year
  group_by(year_numeric, macro_sector) %>%
  summarize(
    estimated_population = sum(perwt, na.rm = TRUE),
    yearly_total = first(yearly_total),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    share_of_workforce = estimated_population / yearly_total,
    macro_sector = factor(
      macro_sector, 
      levels = c(
        "Producer Services", 
        "Social Services", 
        "Personal Services", 
        "Distributive Services", 
        "Construction", 
        "Agriculture", 
        "Other"
      )
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. GENERATE STACKED AREA CHART
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(
  data = plot_industry_trends_clean, 
  aes(
    x = year_numeric, 
    y = share_of_workforce, 
    fill = macro_sector, 
    group = macro_sector
  )
) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.88, color = "white", linewidth = 0.25) + 
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1.0, by = 0.10), 
    limits = c(0, 1.0),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    # Explicitly list every year from 2015 to 2025 on the x-axis
    breaks = 2015:2024,
    limits = c(2015, 2024),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_fill_tableau(palette = "Tableau 10") + 
  labs(
    title = "Workforce Industry Distribution: Marin County Residents",
    subtitle = "Share of employed residents aged 25–64 across macro industry sectors",
    caption = "Data source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS Microdata IPUMS USA (2015–2025). Note: 2020 omitted",
    x = NULL,
    y = "% of Employed Residents",
